p: Nehemiah's Hebrew has 245 singers; Ezra 2:65 has 200. A copying slip in the next line may explain either.

readings.w: Masoretic Text (Leningrad Codex, AD 1008) of Nehemiah; 2 Esdras (Esdras B), the Greek translation of Ezra–Nehemiah, as printed in Rahlfs' edition (Nehemiah = 2 Esdras 11–23; checked on die-bibel.de) (17:67); 1 Esdras 5:41
Ezra 2:65 (Masoretic Text)

why: Each book keeps its own figure, as the Ezra 2:65 variant does. Two slips are possible, and they point opposite ways; see the variant on 7:68. If a copyist's eye ran from the singers' 200 to the mules' 200 ("two hundred and forty-five"), Nehemiah's 245 is really the mules' number and Ezra's 200 is right. If it ran from the singers' 245 to the mules' 245, Nehemiah's 245 is right. The Plain English Translation keeps the Leningrad Codex's 245.

t: A verse missing from the Hebrew
p: Leningrad, most Hebrew manuscripts and Codex Vaticanus lack this verse. It is printed from Ezra 2:66 and Rahlfs' Greek.

readings.w: A few Hebrew manuscripts; the apparatus of BHS; Ezra 2:66; 2 Esdras (Esdras B), the Greek translation of Ezra–Nehemiah, as printed in Rahlfs' edition (Nehemiah = 2 Esdras 11–23; checked on die-bibel.de) (17:68); the KJV and most English Bibles
readings.orig: סוּסֵיהֶם שְׁבַע מֵאוֹת שְׁלֹשִׁים וְשִׁשָּׁה פִּרְדֵיהֶם מָאתַיִם וְאַרְבָּעִים וַחֲמִשָּׁה

readings.w: Masoretic Text (Leningrad Codex, AD 1008) and most Hebrew manuscripts, which go straight from the singers (7:67) to the camels (7:69); Codex Vaticanus (300s AD), as shown in Brenton's English translation of the Greek (1844), which marks the verse as omitted; Jewish Bibles, which number the camels verse 7:68

why: The Plain English Translation prints the verse, following Ezra 2:66, a few Hebrew manuscripts and Rahlfs' Greek text, and keeps the English numbering. The gap is most likely a scribe's eye jump, but there are two ways it could have happened. (1) The singers' number and the mules' number are both 245, so a copyist could skip from the first 245 to the second and lose the horses and mules; then Nehemiah's singers really were 245. (2) Both numbers begin "two hundred," so a copyist could skip from the singers' "two hundred" to the mules' "two hundred and forty-five"; then the singers were 200, as in Ezra 2:65, and the Hebrew's "and forty-five" is the tail of the mules' line. The Plain English Translation keeps the transmitted 245 singers and restores the verse with its 245 mules, which fits view (1); on view (2) the singers' figure would be 200.
b: Because of this missing verse, Hebrew Bibles number the rest of the chapter one lower (Hebrew 7:68–72 = English 7:69–73). The word-by-word Hebrew on this site (STEPBible's edition of the Leningrad Codex) supplies the verse and marks it as a reconstruction; it follows view (2), splitting the singers' number so that its 7:67 shows 200, though the Leningrad Codex itself has 245 there. The Greek is divided: Rahlfs prints the verse, but Codex Vaticanus lacks it (see also the variant on 7:69).

p: The Hebrew, Ezra 2:67 and Rahlfs' Greek have 435 camels and 6,720 donkeys. Codex Vaticanus has only 2,700 donkeys.
